page: Running Hono on Deno JavaScript runtime built on V8. TypeScript support, Deno.serve() for running, Deno Deploy for serverless. Installation: install deno command from official docs. Setup: deno init --npm hono --template=deno my-app, no explicit Hono install needed. Hello World: standard Hono with Deno.serve(app.fetch). Run: deno task start, access http://localhost:8000. Port configuration: Deno.serve({ port: 8787 }, app.fetch). Static files: serveStatic from 'hono/deno' with root, path options. Options: rewriteRequestPath, mimes, onFound, onNotFound, precompressed. Testing: Deno.test with @std/assert, assertEquals. npm vs JSR: Hono available on both, use deno.json imports. Middleware: requires Deno directory syntax, use same registry for type inference. Third-party middleware on JSR recommended. Questions: How do I set up Deno with Hono? How do I serve static files? How do I test? How do I deploy? What's npm vs JSR?

sections.manifest: Deno installation and setup. Install Deno: follow official documentation. Create project: deno init --npm hono --template=deno my-app. Move to project: cd my-app. No explicit dependency install needed (Deno manages it). Questions: How do I install Deno? How do I create project?

Hello World on Deno. File: main.ts. Code: new Hono(), app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Hello Deno!')), Deno.serve(app.fetch). Run: deno task start, access http://localhost:8000. Default port: 8000. TypeScript support without transpile. Questions: What's the entry point? How do I run? What's the default port?
Port configuration. Modify Deno.serve() arguments. Syntax: Deno.serve({ port: 8787 }, app.fetch). Custom port example: 8787. Questions: How do I change port? What's the syntax?

Static file serving with serveStatic. Import from 'hono/deno'. Usage: app.use('/static/*', serveStatic({ root: './' })). Favicon: app.use('/favicon.ico', serveStatic({ path: './favicon.ico' })). Fallback: app.get('*', serveStatic({path: './static/fallback.txt'})). Directory structure: favicon.ico, main.ts, static folder with assets. Questions: How do I serve static files? How do I handle favicon? How do I add fallback?

serveStatic options. rewriteRequestPath: function mapping paths e.g., '/static' to '/statics'. mimes: custom MIME types { m3u8: 'application/vnd.apple.mpegurl' }. onFound: callback when file found, e.g., set Cache-Control header. onNotFound: callback when file not found, logs path. precompressed: checks for .br/.gz files, serves based on Accept-Encoding, prioritizes Brotli > Zstd > Gzip. Questions: How do I rewrite paths? How do I add MIME types? How do I handle caching? How do I add compression?

Deno Deploy serverless platform. Cloud platform for JavaScript/TypeScript. Integrations: GitHub deployment. Management plane for deployment and running. Reference: official Deno Deploy documentation. Questions: What's Deno Deploy? How do I deploy?

Testing on Deno. Framework: Deno.test with assert/assertEquals from @std/assert. Install: deno add jsr:@std/assert. Test syntax: Deno.test('name', async () => {...}). Example: app.request('http://localhost/'), assertEquals(res.status, 200). Run: deno test file.ts. Questions: How do I write tests? How do I assert? How do I run tests?

npm vs JSR package registries. Hono available on both npm and JSR (@hono/hono). deno.json imports configuration. For middleware: use Deno directory syntax import paths. Registry matching: use same registry for Hono and middleware for type inference. JSR recommended for third-party middleware: @hono packages on JSR. npm import: 'npm:hono', JSR import: 'jsr:@hono/hono'. Middleware directory path: 'npm:/hono/' or 'jsr:@hono/hono/'. Example configs for npm and JSR combinations. Questions: Which registry should I use? How do I configure deno.json? When use npm vs JSR? Why use same registry?
